statement: A general pencil of degree-2 plane curves has exactly 3 singular members, each counted once.

source.location: Figure 2, d=2, δ=1; definition of Severi degrees immediately following the figure, printed page 7
source.version: arXiv:0906.3828v4 (18 January 2010), primary PDF inspected 4 November 2026

scope: Singular members of a general projective pencil in the full space of degree-2 plane curves.
notes:
The three singular conics are unions of two distinct lines. This is a discriminant count and includes reducible conics. A general pencil is determined by four general base points; each partition of the four points into two pairs gives one singular conic.

This is the degree-two specialization of the classical homogeneous-discriminant formula, attributed to Boole. Fomin–Mikhalkin Figure 2 is retained as a verification source, not the origin of this count.
